rounds.text: Cresanto Global Limited exhibits severe fundamental distress characterized by an astronomical return on assets of -4000% compared to a sector benchmark of 5.74% [E7]. This catastrophic asset efficiency is compounded by a negative book value of ₹ -7.07, resulting in a negative price-to-book ratio of -0.69x with the share price trading at ₹ 4.88 [E1]. Furthermore, the company offers zero income return to investors, with a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. The negative price-to-earnings ratio of -5.07x stands in stark contrast to the healthy sector benchmark of 31.86x, highlighting deep operational unprofitability [E5]. Conceded: the reported return on equity of 14.26% exceeds the sector benchmark of 10.34% [E8]. However, this isolated metric does little to mask the overarching financial insolvency implied by negative equity and extreme operational destruction.

The bear leans heavily on the catastrophic return on assets of -4000% [E7], but this must be weighed against the company's positive return on equity of 14.26%, which actually outperforms the sector benchmark of 10.34% [E8]. Conceded: the dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E3], but this reflects a micro-cap structure with a market capitalisation of just ₹ 2.08 Cr [E2] rather than a permanent barrier to equity appreciation. While the price-to-earnings ratio is -5.07x against a sector benchmark of 31.86x [E5], the market has already pushed the stock 100% of the way up its 52-week range from a low of 3 to a high of 5 [E4]. Finally, the negative book value of ₹ -7.07 resulting in a -0.69x price-to-book ratio [E1] entirely misses the momentum demonstrated by the stock price sitting at the absolute peak of its annual trading band [E4].

The bull attempts to dismiss the catastrophic return on assets of -4000% by pointing to a positive return on equity of 14.26% [E8], but a massive divergence between asset destruction and equity returns signals profound underlying financial distortion rather than fundamental health. Conceded: the stock sits 100% of the way up its 52-week range [E4], yet trading at the top of a narrow band between 3 and 5 [E4] for a micro-cap of just ₹ 2.08 Cr [E2] offers zero fundamental protection against underlying insolvency. Furthermore, dismissing the negative book value of ₹ -7.07 and the negative price-to-book ratio of -0.69x [E1] as mere missed momentum [E4] ignores the reality that negative equity means liabilities exceed total assets. Finally, citing a lack of dividends as a mere structural quirk of a ₹ 2.08 Cr market capitalisation [E2, E3] obscures the reality of zero capital return for investors backing a business with a P/E of -5.07x [E5].
